podEn: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck
podZh: Matt Turck 的 MAD 播客
tEn: The Largest Chip in History: Cerebras CEO on Why AI Needs Speed
tZh: 史上最大芯片：Cerebras CEO谈AI为何需要速度
sEn: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman discusses why bigger chips are essential for fast AI inference, how GPUs fall short, and the company's remarkable road to the biggest semiconductor IPO ever.
sZh: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman探讨为何更大的芯片对快速AI推理至关重要，GPU为何不足，以及公司如何走到史上最大半导体IPO。

consensus.en: Speed in tokens per second per user is now the dominant measure of AI usefulness and productivity.
consensus.zh: 每秒每用户生成的token数（即速度）现已成为衡量AI实用性和生产力的核心指标。

consensus.en: Inference speed is limited by moving model weights from memory to compute, which Cerebras's SRAM-based wafer-scale chip accelerates.
consensus.zh: 推理速度受限于将模型权重从内存移到计算单元的过程，而Cerebras基于SRAM的晶圆级芯片能极大加速这一环节。

consensus.en: The AI industry faces real shortages in HBM memory, CoWoS packaging, and data center capacity, not demand bubbles.
consensus.zh: AI行业真正面临的是HBM内存、CoWoS封装和数据中心容量的短缺，而非需求泡沫。

consensus.en: The chip landscape is becoming a multi-silicon ecosystem with specialized ASICs (TPU, Trainium, Cerebras) alongside GPUs.
consensus.zh: 芯片格局正演变为多芯片生态，专用ASIC（TPU、Trainium、Cerebras）与GPU共存。

consensus.en: Reasoning and agentic AI increase the importance of fast inference; verification and guardrails add extra compute needs.
consensus.zh: 推理和智能体式AI提升了快速推理的重要性；验证和护栏机制也增加了额外算力需求。

consensus.en: China is a genuine industrial adversary, strong in open-source models and power, but behind in advanced chips.
consensus.zh: 中国是一个真正的产业对手，在开源模型和电力方面领先，但在先进芯片上落后。

contrarian.en: GPUs have a fundamental architectural weakness for fast inference because their decode step is limited by HBM memory bandwidth.
contrarian.zh: GPU在快速推理上存在根本性架构缺陷，因为其解码步骤受限于HBM内存带宽。

contrarian.en: Wafer-scale chips are the clear best approach for AI; bigger chips avoid the industry's most severe constraints like HBM and 3nm.
contrarian.zh: 晶圆级芯片显然是AI的最佳路径；更大的芯片避开了行业最严峻的约束，如HBM和3纳米工艺。

contrarian.en: CUDA's durable moat is disappearing; top labs now train without it, and moving from GPU to Cerebras cloud takes only eight keystrokes.
contrarian.zh: CUDA的持久护城河正在消失；顶级实验室已不用它训练，而从GPU切换到Cerebras云只需八次按键。

contrarian.en: Cerebras's "perfect" IPO timing came after a decade of being ignored; solving the impossible problem in 2020 still drew no buyers.
contrarian.zh: Cerebras“完美”的IPO时机源于被忽视的十年；2020年解决了不可能的问题，却依然无人问津。

contrarian.en: The AI boom is not a bubble: unlike telecom overbuilding, current demand already outstrips supply in memory and data centers.
contrarian.zh: AI繁荣并非泡沫：不同于电信业过度建设，当前内存和数据中心的需求已超过供给。

contrarian.en: GPUs' training advantage is overstated; their need for tensor parallel distributed compute is a barrier that Cerebras avoids with data parallel.
contrarian.zh: GPU的训练优势被夸大了；其张量并行分布式计算的需求是一大障碍，而Cerebras用数据并行规避了这个问题。

turns.en: So maybe to zoom out as the last question—what’s your best guess about where all of this is going? You know, obviously, who knows in AI, but in the next year or two?
turns.zh: 那最后把镜头拉远一点，你猜这一切会走向何方？你知道，在 AI 领域显然没人知道答案，但可以聊聊未来一两年内的趋势？

turns.en: Well, we know some things. We know that the model you’re using today—whether it’s GPT-4 or GPT-5/6—will be the worst model you ever use. And whatever you think is cool about it right now is going to be boring and backwards in six months. And that is so exciting. I watch the way our young engineers use it, and it’s very different from the way I’m using it. It’s a fun time where you can learn from your young team members, because they’re using AI very differently.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们确实知道一些事情。我们知道，你今天用的模型——无论是 GPT-4 还是 GPT-5/6——都会成为你未来用过的最差的模型。无论你现在觉得它多酷，六个月后都会显得无聊和落后。这真的很令人兴奋。我观察我们的年轻工程师使用它的方式，和我自己很不一样。这是一个有趣的时刻，你可以向年轻的团队成员学习，因为他们使用 AI 的方式非常不同。

transcript.sec: AI's impact on SaaS and enterprise data

turns.en: I think the business of dashboarding—and the damage AI is doing to SaaS—is, I think, unrepairable. You can ask your AI to build you a tool like Salesforce, and 30 seconds later you have a working tool. It’s just unbelievable. And all the things that were difficult because they cut across organizational silos, right? But one of the things that’s really hard is if you want to know, for your top-performing people, when was the last time they got a stock option refresh and how much holding power is left. So, how much unvested stock they have left at today’s price?
turns.zh: 我认为仪表盘这类业务——以及 AI 对 SaaS 带来的冲击——几乎无法挽救了。你可以让 AI 帮你建一个类似 Salesforce 的工具，30 秒之后你就能得到一个可用的产品，简直不可思议。过去那些因为跨组织孤岛而困难重重的事情，对吧？但真正难的一点是：如果你想知道你的高绩效人才最近一次拿到股票期权增发是什么时候，以及他们还有多少持股空间——也就是按现价计算还有多少未归属的股票，这是很难查的。

turns.en: There are like five systems. You’re in Workday, you’re in your stock admin.
turns.zh: 大概有五个系统。你在 Workday 里，在你的股票管理系统里。

turns.en: You’re in Carta. None of them can—and that’s what a CEO wants.
turns.zh: 你还要用到 Carta。但没有任何一个系统能打通这些数据——这正是 CEO 想要的。

turns.en: How much holding power for my top guys?
turns.zh: 我的核心员工还有多少持股空间？

turns.en: And I used to have little tools I wrote for this. And boom, I’ve got a little app that I had done in Spark, right?
turns.zh: 我以前会自己写一些小工具来处理这个。然后砰的一下，我用 Spark 就做出了一个小应用，对吧？

turns.en: Well, what a story. It’s just incredible to hear all of this from you. What a journey, and what an exciting future. So, thank you very much. I learned a lot, and this was terrific. Thank you, Andrew.
turns.zh: 哇，真是一个精彩的故事。听到你讲这些，简直难以置信。多么了不起的一段旅程，多么令人兴奋的未来。非常感谢你，我学到了很多，这期节目太棒了。谢谢你，Andrew。

turns.en: Thank you for having me on your show. I really appreciate it.
turns.zh: 感谢你邀请我上节目，我非常感激。

turns.en: Hi, it’s Matt Turk again. Thanks for listening to this episode of the Mad Podcast.
